utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. We understand there may be a procedural matter before we proceed further.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Very briefly, yesterday was the deadline for the Defence to file its response to Prosecution application for consolidated statements. The response was indeed prepared and ready for filing yesterday night. Unfortunately, due to our own forgetfulness, we failed to send it last night on time. We apologise for the forgetfulness of counsel and hope that the Chamber will show some understanding for that matter. This is all we wish to say at this stage. We will also file the Defence response, this time 15 days in advance, for the Prosecution application to submit a third report for Mr. Eichner. That's all for us. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, is there any concern.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No concern on that matter, Your Honour. While we're discussing procedural matters, with your leave, I also have one to discuss.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can we just say we appreciate frankness, Mr. Mettraux, and you may be sure that we will take notice of the filing.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could we very briefly move into private session to discuss a matter which involves some witnesses, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, the next witness will be led by colleague, Matthias Neuner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I just confirm that the two witnesses you were speaking were programmed to be here on Thursday, the 24th.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We've got the right ones. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. When you have put the head phones on, would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that is given to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're most welcome. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, I believe Mr. Neuner has some questions for you, sir

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your name is Ismail Ramadani?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And your ethnicity is Albanian?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you live in the village of Ljuboten in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the witness's other microphone can be turned on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could the second microphone please be turned on, of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, you provided two written statements to the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY, did you?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Da. [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in April of this year, a female colleague and myself, we met you in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And on that occasion, you signed another statement containing parts of those earlier statements?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. There was some mistakes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I will address that in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I may ask the usher to take the following documents to the witness, please. The first statement could please be placed on the ELMO, please. If could you please zoom in or show the signature also.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, on the first page on the bottom in the middle, do you recognise your signature?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And upon providing that statement, you signed each and every page of that statement?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if you could please turn to page 16 of that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: There's a witness declaration here, or a witness acknowledgment. Did you sign that acknowledgment, Mr. Ramadani?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If the statement could please be removed and the second document shown on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And once you were giving us this first statement, Mr. Ramadani, you had the opportunity to provide corrections and additions?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And all these additions and corrections were noted down in this second document.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if you please look at the on first page at the signature, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you signed each and every page of that document?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if you could please turn, Mr. Usher, to page 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, did you sign here on this page on the upper part, the witness acknowledgment?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And on the lower part as well, if you may have a look?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And, together, do both statements contain what you would say if you would testify today in this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. They both contain what I would say today.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would ask to tender both statements into evidence, please, under -- under Rule 92 ter, please. Your Honours, we have prepared binders containing some exhibits, and if I could impose one more time of the goodwill of the usher to hand them over to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I say, Mr. Neuner, that the object of the order of the Chamber was to have one statement which was the 92 ter statement. We come close to having two statements again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. We made internally the decision to merge both statements, meaning both prior statements of this witness, into the consolidated 92 ter statement; and upon seeing this witness, he had to make certain additions or corrections. The second statement, which is in front of the Chamber, makes explicit reference to each paragraph or each relevant paragraph of this consolidated statement, and, therefore, we kept it separate so as to indicate what the 92 ter statement is and what the additions and corrections this witness had on the day we saw him are.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we may assist, I can indicate that we have mentioned in our filing of today, which should have been of yesterday, that we would not object to the addendum and corrigendum being tendered pursuant to Rule 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It does occur to us that it may be convenient to the Defence to be able to readily see where there have been changes in the last week or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. The two statements will be received separately.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Statement with ERN N006-4049 will become Exhibit P188. Statement with N0006-4037 will become Exhibit P189, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I could please ask that the statement is to be admitted under seal because this witness mentions also some of the protected witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Both will be received under seal. Could we indicate as a procedural matter for the future we're conscious that one of the effects of the 92 ter procedure, and for that matter 92 bis with cross-examination, and any tendering of a straightforward 92 bis statement, one effect is that members of the public present in court and members of the wider public who may be taking notice of these proceedings have no indication of the general effect of the evidence of the witness. The Chamber is aware that other Chambers follow a procedure of asking the party tendering the statement to make a very concise summary orally by counsel of the essential points of the statement that is tendered. We think there are advantages to the wider public in that being down; and as long as the statement is concise, it will not introduce any significant use of time, and we would therefore want to adopt that procedure. We realise it will be necessary for a little time to be allowed for thought to be given to a summary by counsel. So we don't ask that it be done at this moment, Mr. Neuner. But perhaps even tomorrow it may be possible for that to be observed with witnesses that may be called tomorrow and thereafter. That will, of course, apply to any Defence witness that is following the 92 bis or ter procedure as well, looking ahead. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would be in a position to give a brief summary; however, this witness has been at one location which I would mention only in private session. Is this agreeable to you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would be excellent. Thank you. When we come to a certain location, we can take that in private session and then move back into public, if that is what you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I will proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani has been on the weekend, the 10th and 12th of August, 2001, in Ljuboten. And on the Sunday, the 12th of August, 2001, he has been at the cellar of one house, which I will mention in private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could that be done at the end of your summary?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It will be, Your Honours. And he was there together with a group of ten persons, and the forces of the Republic of Macedonia did enter the yard and took this group out of the cellar or asked the group to come out of the cellar and searched them. The group was taken to a ramp in front of the compound, mistreated there, and asked to walk to a checkpoint at the border between Ljuboten and Ljubanci. And at this point in time, the witness believes to have seen Mr. Boskoski. From there, the witness was brought to the police station in Mirkovci, and thereafter he was brought to the hospital, the city hospital in Skopje. And from the city hospital in Skopje, he was brought to the court in Skopje, and thereafter to the Sutka prison. And on 10 December 2001, he was released from Sutka prison. If we could now move into private session, I would just mention the location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, was this an adequate summary of your testimony, which I just tried to provide?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have prepared binders containing exhibits. If I could impose one more time on the goodwill of the usher to hand them over to the Court and to the witness. If we could please move to tab 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise what you see in this photo?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is a weekend house called Brace's House. This is where Boskoski was. The gates at the time were own.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: For the record, this is exhibit with 65 ter number 199. ERN number of that photo was N004-4571.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it not already an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I have more information that the 65 ter number 199.14.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Our concern is with exhibit numbers in this trial. I think it is an exhibit with some markings. If it's not been separately tendered, well, then, we will receive it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It is annotated by protected witness M-017, so if I could kindly ask to tender that again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you please --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P190, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Then I would move on to the next exhibit. This is tab 3 your binders, 65 ter number is 490. The English ERN number is N005-0480 till N005-0481. Could this be displayed in e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This is already Exhibit P108, I believe, Mr. Neuner. As soon as that technical difficulty which keeps reoccurring is corrected, we will have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We can also work from the hard copies. If the usher could please take the document from tab 3. Tab 3. Tab 3, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, this is a document from Cair police department. Have you seen that document before?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I would tell you that on the first page in the middle your name Ismail Ramadani is mentioned, do you find your name?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I can see my name, yes. But the document contains misinformation, and the content of this document has no value for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I will come to that in a moment. If you could please take this step by step, Witness. You found your name, yes?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we please move into private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could please move to tab 2, the photo, with the ERN N004-5201, 65 ter number 199.18.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this picture?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is the Mirkovci police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: We were brought here, in the garage of this police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. You're pointing at the right garage of the two?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: In the first one, to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If could I ask -- if I could ask to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P191, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you could please move to tab 4, 65 ter number is 220. The ERN number is N000-5176, and we need to look, please, at the third page of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is a medical report from the General Hospital Skopje, mentioning your name. Do you find your name on the upper part?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, it's here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since there are some problems in e-court, we are not able to see the documents that my learned colleague is showing to the witness at all. They are being received. We don't think we will have any complaints on that, but we simply could not see what the witness is shown and what is tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. I know that attention is being given to the technical problem at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We can place the document on the ELMO so it is by ELMO technology available. If could I please ask the usher to place the third page after that document on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: On the upper left-hand side, you said already you find your name, Ismail Ramadani, there, yes?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And it states here you were admitted on the 13th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Admitted to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if we look at the first main paragraph, it mentions there that you had a serious fracture of the 2nd to the 8th ribs on your left side, and fractures of the 7th, 8th, and 10th ribs on your right side. My question is: Is the description of your injuries correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: You men if it's correct? No. I wouldn't say so. I have more ribs that were broken, and here it mentions only a few.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It mentions the 2nd --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my apologies for interrupting. But in the left-hand corner it says is that it is a medical report from 14th of November, 2003, which is two years after the event. That's what I want the to point out. Are these injuries that took place after the event? You can see that in the lower left corner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It is a report, on the face of it, provided on the 14th of November, 2003, dealing with the condition of the patient on the 13th of August, 2001, clearly prepared from hospital records. So on the face of it, that is what it is. It is not dealing with injuries in November 2003 but dealing with injuries in November 2001 [sic].

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I just wanted to point out to this fact. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The injuries I should have said were in August 2001. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If could you now move on to the second main paragraph, it says here: "Bruising to the head," in the third line. Did you, upon admission on the 13th of August, 2001, did you have bruisings to your head?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: One bruising or bruisings?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Many, I would say. I would not be able to count them right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I can ask to have this document admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 192, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we can move to the next document under tab 5. ERN number is N006-3719 till N006-3733, and the 65 ter number is 1004. Can it be please be placed, the first page on the ELMO. Since it is shown to the witness, we may wish to -- there is a B/C/S part of this document at roughly the middle of that tab. We can show the first page of this B/C/S or Macedonian original version, please. This is after a green -- after a green paper. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you find your name on the upper left-hand side, Mr. Ramadani?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, it's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And below that it says that your father is Muharem and your mother is Sabrije?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And it also talks about the fact that you were admitted on the 13th of August, 2001, in that document, to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If could I ask that this document is please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P193, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could please move on to the next photograph in tab 7 of the binder. ERN number -- there are two photographs of the first photo. The ERN number of the first photo is N005-7597, and the 65 ter number is 1029. If you could please move it a little bit upwards, Mr. Usher, also out. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who is depicted on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: It's me, and I still have the scars. And if you want me to, I can show it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We have the picture.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Where is the scar?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we please zoom in a little bit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The scars are on my back. They have been caused by a knife. There is a vertical and horizontal line.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can the technician please zoom in a little bit. Thank you. Can you please move it up a little bit, the picture. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please encircle -- Because it's difficult to see here on the electronic display, could you please encircle with a marker the scar?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I can't see the marker.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you please add today's date and your signature below?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Could you please remind what date it is today.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The 17th of May, 2007.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if we could please move to the next picture with ERN N005-7602.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What do you see here?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I see the scars that was caused by knife.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you please sign and add today's date.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we please tender those pictures? Can I please tender both pictures into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The first picture, bearing ERN N005-7597 will become Exhibit P194. The second picture, ERN N005-7602, will be Exhibit P195, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Finally, I wish to show you a short video excerpt. The exhibit number is 21, 65 ter number 309. If you recognise anybody, please tell us to stop and we will do so.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you recognise anybody?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. Ljube Boskoski and his body-guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Where was Ljube Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber has not seen anything of this yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. We will play it again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we could also see that the witness has nothing on his screen although he responded to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can this please be checked.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Ljube Boskoski, and this here is his body-guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: There were two persons shown on the video. Could you say where was Ljube Boskoski and where was the body-guard?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. Ljube Boskoski was the person who was pointing at something with his finger.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was he on the right or on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I think on the left-hand side, as I view it from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we show that again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This one here is Ljube Boskoski, while the other person is his body-guard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Unfortunately, each person was at one time on the left and at another time on the right. So you will have so try something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What colour was the clothes Mr. Boskoski was wearing?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: A black jacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you tendering the video?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It's already admitted as Exhibit P21, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: When you're ready, Ms. Residovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Ramadani. My name is Edina Residovic, and together with my colleague, Guenael Mettraux, I'm defending Mr. Ljube Boskoski. You have given certain information earlier about which my learned colleague has asked you, and I would only like to confirm that you were born on 8th of February, 1965 in Ljuboten; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you have been living in Ljuboten for the entire time?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your family as well as the -- a number of families in Ljuboten was numerous. You had seven children in the house, and then you had two brothers and four sisters in addition. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the event -- events in 2001, you were married and had two children.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. At that time I had two children. Now I have three.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the question of my colleague you already said that you have given two statements before to the investigators of the Prosecutor. Is it correct, Mr. Ramadani, that you gave a statement to the representatives of the OSCE before that?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. About the two statements, that is true. Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also gave a statement to the International Red Cross Committee; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All the statements that you talked about with my learned colleagues and that were given to the investigator of the Prosecutor were given with the assistance of the Albanian interpreter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And each time you have been signing the statements, confirming that everything that you have said is the truth and to the best of your recollection to the events; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The president of your village or of the Crisis Staff, Kenan Salievski, was the link between you and the other villagers with the representatives of the Prosecutor of the ICTY; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Salievski, yes. Yes. He informed us at times.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when you were giving the statements to the investigator of the ICTY, where were you usually giving those statements?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I gave the statements in my village, in our village, Ljuboten, I think at the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me if it is correct that there are -- there were several persons giving statements on the same day.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours. Can we please clarify on which day or which year we are talking about, because there were several statements the witness gave.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about the two previous statements that he recognised and that were later put in the -- into the consolidated list. The statements that he had given in 2003. Thank you, I apologise. Let me just have some water.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, you can surely confirm that your village of Ljuboten is on the slopes of Skopska Crna Gora and that you can see Skopje very well in the valley below from that position.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That position of the village is of an exceptional strategic importance for the city of Skopje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Above the village, so above the Ljubotenski Bacila and Basinec, there is an old road that is called Muralovo Dzade or Sultanovo Dzade, by the people; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is the road that could connect Kumanovo area with the Tetovo area and with the Kosovo border; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I think this road is a connection road that links or connects the Kumanovo area with Kosovo. There is no connection with Tetovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Directly below Muralovo Dzade, there is the location called Crn Kamen, from which you could completely see the area of Kumanovo, but also the border towards Kosovo and the area of Tetovo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: From as I see it, you cannot see them. Because Tetovo is far, you cannot see Tetovo from there. Kumanovo, too, is several kilometres far from Crna Kamen.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You probably have a better overview of the situation than I do. Is it correct that directly behind the mountain there is the village of Matejce where in 2001, during the events in Ljuboten, the headquarters of the NLA brigade thought that area was located?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: It is true that it is behind the mountain of Matejce.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The fact that Ljuboten is located not far from the borders and that it has strategic importance during the crisis in Macedonia, is it correct that the army of the Republic of Macedonia deployed at positions around the village, and, in that way, secured the space of around 20 kilometres from the Kosovo and Serbia borders?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. I think this is correct. It was there before the event happened. The village was surrounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the events in Ljuboten, through the media and possibly in some other ways, you learned that the groups of Albanian terrorists have attacked police stations, police patrols, and the positions of the army of the Republic of Macedonia in several locations. Did you have any such information?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No. This is not correct. This is misinformation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Ramadani, that the Albanian population of Ljuboten was approving the actions that the NLA was performing on the territory of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You personally were approving of the actions of the NLA.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I think, to be frank, I liked the NLA, but I did not participate. I was not a member.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Ramadani, that the village, apart from the strategic importance for the city of Skopje, was also quite convenient for the logistic support for the NLA forces that were fighting in the background of the village?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No. This is not correct. There was no logistics whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that as early as in the spring 2001, armed representatives of NLA arrived to the village and requested that the young people from the village join NLA?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No. That's not correct. The village was totally unprotected.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that some of the younger men from the village director joined NLA and participated in the actions of NLA?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: That's not correct. I have no knowledge about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, the president of the Crisis Staff at the village was Kenan Saliu or Kenan Salievski; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If, in his statements to the investigators of the OTP, Kenan Salievski would say that, from the village of Ljuboten, member so NLA were Suat Saliu, Riza Junuzi, Besim Muretazani, Rafiz Bajrami, Shefajet Bajrami, Fikret Aliu, Nimet Aliu, Ruhan Jashari, Ramadan Alimi who was killed in the fights around Matejce, Musa Salimi, Refadim Salimi, Faik Murati, Shefqet Murati, Zeqir Murati, Rasim Murati, and others. While in the village inside, there were Commander Musko, Commander Lisi, and others?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Commander Miskoja.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You would certainly be able to confirm that this information was correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No. There was no Commander Miskoja or Lisi in the village. This is all misinformation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware -- are you familiar with the name Halimi Baki?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. I know him as a teacher. Not in any other capacity.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you also know him by the name of the Commander Lisi.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: He was not a commander. This is misinformation that was spread. He is a teacher.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You must also know your fellow villager, Fatmir Kamberi.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I know him as a person, but he was not a commander either.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But he was known as Miskoja. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. He was not a commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, as in accordance with the traditional customs of Albanian people, it was normal and usual that every family would have weapons that are otherwise used in celebrations and other events. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: This cannot be said for present times. This may apply to ancient times, because now we use books and we are dedicated to learning, not to using weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 2001, in August, during the events also, you knew that Shefajet Bajrami known also as Shef, belonged to the group of the Commander Teli, who was again a personal friend to the Commander Arusha; do you know that.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I know him as a person, but it is not correct that he was commander or participant. He worked in Italy.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And his brother, Rafiz Bajrami, was in the 114th Brigade of the NLA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. I think that he, too, are worked in Italy at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You must have heard that at the beginning of August in 2001 in Skopje, that Commander Teli was killed with some of his fellow fighters. Have you heard about that?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. It is correct that we heard about this. He was killed in Skopje.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters report: There is a lot of noise in our earphones.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We also hear the noise, but we don't know where it comes from.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, do you know that after the demise of Commander Teli in Skopje, his friend, Commander Arusha, decided to retaliate and place mines; and in the placing of mines, Shefajet Bajrami participated as well?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No. I have no information about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that on the 10th of August, when in Ljubotenski Bacila, land-mines were placed, Shefajet Bajrami, together with some other people, the Commander Malisheva and other armed members of the NLA, entered the village?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No. I don't know about this. This is, as I said, misinformation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Because you aware of the information that you had, that it was the NLA that planted the mine, you personally and your fellow villagers as early as Friday -- as on the Friday you felt unsafe enough, there was fear spreading among the people. So there were movements of the villagers of Ljuboten. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. We heard about this incident, but it happened far from the village, about five [as interpreted] kilometres far from the village. It was high in the mountains where it happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Despite that, part of the villagers, some 50 families, left the village, together with the children.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes that's correct. They left because of the gunshots that were being heard from all sides of the village, and there was no other way out for them.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Line 19 should read 15 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you and the other grown-up men, upon being summoned from the Commander Lisi, met and discussed what would be the way to react in the village is searched?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No. There was no meeting whatsoever. We were civilians, unprotected civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Ramadani, that on the 12th, there was cross-fire between the people who were armed in the village and the forces that were entering the village?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: In my opinion, the people in the village had no weapons whatsoever. All the shots and shelling came from the other side, from the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, is it correct that, actually, throughout the crisis in Macedonia it was only on that date, the 12th, that there would be certain -- that there were certain military or combat activities inside the village. Is that correct? There were -- there were no activities of such sort on any other day, inside the village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I know that there was no combat activity in the village. Only a massacre committed by the Macedonian police happened in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like you to answer my question. Is it only one day when there was something happening related to use of weapons. Was it only on the 12th? Is it only on that date, not before and not afterwards, there were forces entering the village?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Let me explain. The gunshots were heard not only on one day. They were heard as of that Friday. The shelling and the gunshots continued for three days, and I think it was on the second day that the Macedonian police entered the village, on the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know the name Muzafer Agushi from Aracinovo?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, I know him, but I'm not related to him in any way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You know that he was killed in Ljuboten, and that it was published in the books about NLA?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I think that he was not killed in Ljuboten village. He was killed in the mountains. And as I explained, the mountain is about 15 kilometres far from Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask that the witness is now shown 65 ter number 1D74. Your Honours, we are not sure if the e-court is in operation, so we are prepared a hard copy. So I would like to ask the usher to help us show this document to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll very grateful that have you the hard copies. We have only three minutes remaining of this session. Do you want to move on to this now or have the break first?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe this would be the right time to take a break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We'll resume then at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Mr. President, I have been informed that e-court is now operational, so since we have in addition to the fact that we have shown the hard copy. Can we show this document 65 ter number 1D74, page 1D1041, and the English translation 1047. Your Honours, just to clarify, I would like to say that we received the documents under Rule 68; and since it is in Albanian, we have asked the CLSS to only translate the relevant parts. The first page is the page saying that this is the book speaking about the NLA Kosovo, the Kosovo liberation army. I would like to ask that the second page is also shown, 1D1042, that is English 1D1048. That is a monography of the type members of the Kosovo Liberation Army. Please show page 1D1043, the English 1D1049; whereby, it could be seen who is the publisher and who are the persons that were writing this publication. Please show 1D1044, and English 1D1050. This is only the title of the book, "The Kosovo Liberation Army Martyrs," published in Pristina in 2001. And I would like 1D1046, at the same time showing, 1D1052. Your Honours, behind the monography, from page 17 to page 104, there's a list of all the deceased members of the NLA; and in the first line that you see here, we have translated the words found at the top of each page above the columns, and they represent the full name of the deceased person, the year of birth, place of birth, year of death, and the place of death. This is only about persons died, as it is mentioned in the book for persons that there are data, precise data about.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, the image that you have in front of you now, in the list of names at the fourth -- position four, do you see the name of Muzafer Agushi, about whom I have asked you a little bit before the break? Can you see that name written there?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No. I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the Albanian, the fourth name written in this name list, do you see it now?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No. It's not there. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This person is born in 1981 in Aracinovo; and in the next column, which speaks about the year of death, it says 2001, and the place of death is Ljuboten. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Not correct. He was not killed in Ljuboten. He was killed somewhere up in the mountains about 15, 1-5, kilometres away from the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you also see that the year and place are written as an information of the death of Muzafer Agushi; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. The year is there, 2001.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we would now ask that document is tendered as an exhibit of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D7, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, you know also (redacted); is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I know him. He is a co-villager of mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is a (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 12th of August, 2001, he also had possessed weapons?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No. He did not have any weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I don't wish to interrupt but the person who was just mentioned is a protected witness, if this please could be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Redaction. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On that day, he escaped towards the woods and was wounded; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. He was wounded by the Macedonian police.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And he is a NLA member; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No. He was not a member of the NLA. He was an ordinary civilian.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, I will ask you a few things about which you spoke briefly with my learned colleague the Prosecutor, and you have been mentioning that in your previous statements, especially in the corrections you've provided in April when -- when it was the last time you spoke to the colleagues from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask knew we show document 1D --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- 1D48, page 1D00595, and the Macedonian version 1D0607.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before I ask you about what is written in your changes, is it correct that once you were taken out of the house you were in, that you were immediately ordered to put your T-shirts over your heads and to -- and to lay on the floor?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During the entire time you were lying on the ground, you had to have your T-shirts over your heads?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, it is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, while moving from the Ljuboten towards the Brace's House, you were not allowed to take the -- your shirts off your heads; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No, we were not allowed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you could better hear some words than to personally see; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. We could hear, but we couldn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the documents, the last changes that made by the end of April in Ljuboten, in point 5, you have said that you had your T-shirt over your head and, therefore, was not able to see anything. But what you have seen, as it is mentioned there, and I would like to ask you whether that is true, you have seen only the colours of some of the insignia of the uniforms and that was that have you seen black and blue. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. I think when they got us out of the basement, we could see it then, but then they ordered us to put our T-shirts over our heads.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, practically, when our learned colleagues showed you some uniforms, you were only able to say that what you have seen resembles what you were shown; is that correct? I apologise. I read line 3 in this paragraph 9, which says that you were shown a photograph of the uniforms, and then you say: "Some of them look like in the picture ERN number N004-5059." Is it correct that you were not completely certain to tell whether they are-- whether they are identical or not, but that it looked like to what you have seen at that time. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I think that these uniforms were there, and both the special police forces and the reservist -- reserve forces were present on Sunday in the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Mr. Ramadani, regardless of the fact that you have served army in the past, because of the things you were doing in your life, you did not know the precise structure of the army and of the police of the Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I couldn't know that of the Macedonian army because I -- I did my military service in the Yugoslav police, so earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So not only that you were not in the Macedonian army, you never served any duties in the Macedonian police as well; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Given your position and your expertise that is not connected to the competences of certain body, you did not precisely know the competences that certain Ministries have in the Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I don't know these.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you know that the investigating judge and the investigating judges in Macedonia are those carrying out the investigations for certain crimes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: This I know, that they carry investigations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also know that the prosecutors and their responsibility to conduct the business of the prosecutors' office are linked to the Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Macedonia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in 2001, the Minister of Justice was Mr. --

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I think it was Hixhet Mehmeti.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- Hixhet Mehmeti, an Albanian; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, in your statements, you have been explaining also about your experience in the Sutka prison. Is it correct that you do not know whose members are the guards in that prison, the prisoner guards, nor what are the bodies that are superior to the Sutka prison and the personnel of the prison. Have you no personal knowledge about these things. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: That's correct. I don't have any knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now ask to move into private session, since I will be mentioning probably names of some persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Ramadani, that while you were inside the police station Mirkovci, the police called police [as interpreted] twice to check the health status of the detainees?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. We didn't undergo any medical treatment there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Together with several other persons you were transferred to the hospital to be given medical care; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, but on the second night, not on the first night, which means 13th of August. They came at around 6.00 p.m., and they took several persons and took them to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before, according doctor's instruction, you were transferred to the hospital, Atulla Qaili was transferred before you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Atulla Qaili was transferred there the night before.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the hospital, you were rendered adequate medical care; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: First of all, the Macedonian reserve forces ill-treated us, even at the hospital. They made us take off our civilian clothes, and they put pyjamas on us. They ill-treated us, and then after that they sent us to the rooms.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The doctors in the hospital offered you appropriate medical care; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: The doctors at the hospital gave us only IV treatment; then they tied our wounds, the wounds that we had on our heads and faces. Only that, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So if the medical records, that my learned colleague has shown you, it is stated that you were administered all necessary medications, then this would not be correct -- correctly written. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: This is not correct. I told here a little bit before, they only gave us IV treatment, two bottles of IV medication; and then the following day, on the 13th of August, a bottle of IV medication. And as I said here before, they gave us a treatment -- applied a cream on our wounds, and one of the doctors said that, "You can't heal immediately, so you need several applications of this cream." But then somebody from the court came to ask questions to us, and then they tied our hands and sent us to the Sutka prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you left detention, Mr. Ramadani, you never filed criminal charges against any person who ill-treated you in Ljuboten, inside the police station or in the hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No. We didn't press any charges.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You never asked your attorney to file such charges, criminal charges on your behalf. Is that correct as well?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I think that we didn't have a lawyer. The lawyers that you were assigned to us were assigned by the other party. So they were state attorney, and they didn't have any interest in us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "the other side," would it be correct if I said that you were assigned an ex officio attorney, the one retained for you by the court? Is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. I was assigned an ex officio attorney by the court, but I only see him once in the four months that I was in prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Ramadani, that when you left detention, you were mistrustful of the police and the Macedonian authorities, and that was the reason why you refused to give any statements or to file any charges to those bodies? Was that the reason why you never gave a statement or filed charges?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, it is true. I didn't trust in them. That's the reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You trusted only the international organisations. So your statements about the actual events in Ljuboten and what happened to you personally were given only to the OSCE and the International Committee of the Red Cross and the investigators of this Tribunal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. I gave a statement only to them, to no one else.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You believed that that was enough, and that they had the duty, if that was necessary, to inform the Macedonian authorities about your statements; is that correct? I didn't hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Can you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You trusted that it was enough to give statements to the international organisations, and you believed that it is their duty to inform the Macedonian authorities about your statements, if that was necessary. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Ramadani.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have concluded the cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Residovic. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. Your Honours, today I will ask questions of the witness, Ismail Ramadani, and I will comprise the issues that my learned colleague, Edina Residovic, did not comprise in her cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation], Mr. Ramadani, my name is Antonio Apostolski and together with my distinguished colleague, Jasmina Zivkovic, are Defence counsels for Mr. Johan Tarculovski. I will ask you to today about the events in Ljuboten in 2001, the 10th, 11th and 12th of August. Can we start asking questions?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You have completed primary education in your mother tongue, the Albanian; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you speak the Macedonian language?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You live with your family, your wife and children; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your consolidated 92 ter statement of 25th of April, 2007, 2D2388, page 2, paragraph 4, line 3, you state that: "I have been a supporter of the NLA in 2001, but I never participated actively in the war as a fighter, as a combatant." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. I was not member. Now when you say "supporter," anybody would support his own side. That's why I was such a supporter.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell us in which way you supported the NLA?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I have no comment to this effect. I did complete my education, but I was not employed. I worked as a farmer.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I apologise, but you failed to answer my question. Can you tell us in what way have you supported the NLA?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: In no way.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your consolidated 92 ter statement of the 25th of April, 2007, 2D2388, page 2, paragraph 4, line 4, you say: "I think that in the village there were around 40 Albanian houses that were supporters, as I was." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I may well have said this, but I don't know concretely who was among these 40 households that you mentioned, who supported and who didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: How many houses of Albanians are there in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I think 300, around 300 houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that Ljuboten is a small village where people know one another?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Well, in my opinion, it's not that small, where everyone can know everyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. In your consolidated 92 ter statement of 25th April, 2007, 2D2388, page 3, paragraph 6, you say that you remember that on the morning of Friday, the 10th of August, shelling of the village started; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I was harvesting tobacco in the field at 6.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Further, in paragraph 7 of the same statement, you continue by saying that: "The shelling was coming from the direction where the APCs and the cannons were located." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And that they - you referred to APCs [as interpreted] and cannons - were not further than 100 metres away from the village, and that you were able to see them clearly. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. They were above the village. They were positioned above the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in the transcript line 17 in the translation, I see that it is translated as "APC," while I was asking about a "tank."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You were also able to see that the Macedonian army was present on those locations because you recognised them by their uniforms; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I ask that the witness is shown the photograph 65 ter ERN N005-7605. I think we could zoom out a bit so that we see a larger panorama, so that we could see a broader panorama.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So can you show on the photograph where were the tanks located, and could you mark that with number 1; and then mark with the number 2 where the cannons were located?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. Here. They were positioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: If you need, then the photograph could be zoomed back in.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mark with the number 1 the positions of the cannons.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: To be clear, I was not there nearby, but I know that here, there were tanks and cannons and mortars of the army positioned there, and they were firing uninterruptedly in the direction of the village with all these military equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So could you mark that point with the number 1.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. Here is number 1, and here number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So number 1 marks the location of the tanks, and the number 2 is the location of the cannons; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So the number 2 marks now the location of the mortars.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. Number 1 is the position of the tanks, and 2 the position of the mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this photograph as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D14, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the addendum or correction to the 92 ter statement of Ismail Ramadani of 25th of April, 2007, 2D2422, page 2, paragraph 4, line 3, you state that the shelling lasted from the Friday until the Sunday; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know maybe on the Friday, the 10th of August, 2001, in the morning, where was it that the shells fell?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: To what I know, the first shell fell near my neighbourhood, when the little Erxhan Aliu was killed, at Zija Ahmeti's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you want to say that this happened on the Friday, early in the morning?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I think, Friday morning. I don't know the exact hour, but it was around 8.00 or 9.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us the names of the persons, owners of the houses where the shells fell on the Friday morning.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Well, I think, I know that several people know where the shells fell and I can show --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: I know the houses of several people.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know where they fell?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, I know. I can be correct about three shells, where they fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell me those?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, I can. But I can't --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Just the names of the people, could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, if it is zoomed in, I can show. The first shell fell on -- at the wall of Zija Ahmeti's house. The second shell fell at the house of Ismail Mahmuti's. The third shell fell at Nuredin Elezovski house. So I'm sure about these three shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were there any other shells that fell in the village on the Friday morning but you don't recall where they fell?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: There are other shells. Some other shells fell in the fields and in gardens, but there were no damages to other houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So there was damages to those houses that you have mentioned, damage caused by the shelling.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: There is more damage; but for what I was sure, I showed here.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Your consolidated statement 92 ter of 25th April 2007, 2D2388, page 4, paragraph 9, you state that you and your family stayed home, meaning until 18, 1900 hours on the Saturday evening; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: On Saturday, yes, we were at our home. That's correct. The second night we went to (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Okay. Can you explain why did you move to (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just have the name of the person redacted from the transcript, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And this exhibit is an exhibit under seal as well, if I'm correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you explain why you moved to that house?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, I can. We moved to that house because we were not safe in our basement, so we went to (redacted) to be safe from the shelling from the Macedonian police --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Macedonian army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt my learned colleague again, but the name of the person has just been mentioned again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Apostolski, if you would be careful not to be mentioning the name of the person; and if you, Mr. Ramadani, would try and avoid mentioning the name of the people in the house where you were in the basement or the names of the people who were with you in the basement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Wasn't your house safe although the village has been shelled for two days, on the Friday and the Saturday, by the Macedonian security forces, and you stayed those two days in your basement?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. We stayed in our house only on the first day; then when the shelling started, we tried to go to a safer place because a shell fell in the yard of my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your consolidated 92 ter statement of 25th of April, 2007, 2D2388, page 5, paragraph 13, line 2, you say that: "I saw through a small window of my shelter, I saw the soldiers coming into the village and there were at least 300 soldiers and police officers." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, 100 per cent correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we move into a private session for a while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- to mark the window with the number 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have already marked it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could the witness mark with the number 2 the fence around the house.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: You mean the yard where they took us out from the basement? This is the line we followed, and then they made us lie down. This is number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you put an arrow towards the direction of the gate to the yard of the house?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: The gate is not shown here. It's a bit further. It's not here, but it's towards this side.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you put an arrow when you would get out of the window to which direction the gate is? Which direction would you move?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: It's the direction of the door, after this, or behind this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Once you left the basement, did you go to the direction that you have just shown towards the gate?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No. When they took us out of the basement, they made us lie down on the ground, here, for five or ten minutes, first of all. They took our papers, our identification papers, they made us lie down, and they tortured us. They hit us on our heads and they kicked us, so they tortured us. That's the first thing that they did to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does it mean that with number 2 you have marked the place you were at once you left the basement?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: That is correct, here. Number 2 is here. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you mark with the number 3 the place where the gate to the door is, or the direction in which the gate to the door is, to be more precise?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. This is the arrow towards the door. It's number 3 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: It should be the gate to the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D16, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said that for your own safety from the shelling, you put boxes at the door of the basement.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did in any way you protected yourself, so you're not hurt by the shells through the window?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: We didn't put anything against the window because the shelling was coming behind the house and the window was on the other side of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your 92 ter consolidated statement of 25th of April, 2007, 2D2388, page 5, paragraph 14, line 1, you say that on the 12th of August, 2001, at 10.00 in the morning, "I noticed around 50 police officers in the yard of the house." I'll avoid mentioning the name. It is the aforementioned house that we spoke about. "There was a clock in the basement, so therefore I know that -- that was exactly 10.00."

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So you insist that you have seen the clock?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
