utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And that is the exact time when the police entered the door [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, could we move into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski, we must now have the second break and we will resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm sorry that the break had to be longer than planned because of the need to complete the tape editing, which took longer. Could the Chamber mention, and ask that from tomorrow the matter be observed by all counsel, from now on it will be important where a document being referred to has become an exhibit to refer to the document by the exhibit number rather than earlier numbers, because we need to know whether we're dealing with an exhibit that is under seal or an exhibit that is not under seal; and if references are made bake to earlier numbers there can be a mistake and that can lead to information becoming public that should not. So if we could ask counsel from now on to be very careful, that they look at and refer to exhibit numbers rather than other numbers, where a document is already an exhibit. Thank you for that. Now, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have just few more questions to ask of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct, Mr. Ramadani, that the public prosecutor's office of Skopje filed an indictment against you with regards to the events in Ljuboten on the 10th, 11th, and 12th of August?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. They pressed charges.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Court did not acquit you?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: That's not true. I was acquitted after four months.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were you acquitted by the Court?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the president, Boris Trajkovski, made a decision to pardon the individuals, members of NLA deprived of liberty, pardoned you?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. We received the pardon via a document, and his signature is on the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This means that the Court acquitted you on the basis of the decision on pardoning by -- by Boris Trajkovski?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the witness can be shown 65 ter number 12, ERN N000-4409.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you confirm that this is the decision by which the president, Boris Trajkovski, pardoned you as a member of the so-called NLA?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: This is the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's Exhibit P48.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I would have an if you question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: First of all, I wish to clarify the transcript on page 43, lines 11 and 12, it says, referring to the answer of a witness, "I could see a limited," and this should read, as far as I have understood the translation, "I could see a little bit."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Witness, I want to ask you briefly about the state hospital or the hospital in Skopje. You mentioned - and this is on page 42, line 22 - "The Macedonian reserve forces ill-treated us even at the hospital."

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What forces are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Police forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to take you to questions from my learned colleagues - and this is page 54 to 57 of the transcript - referring to the view from the cellar, meaning the window and so on?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If please Exhibit 2D16 could be shown again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You told us earlier today that from time to time you left the cellar --

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: -- on that Sunday, the 12th of August. Can you tell me where did you go when you left the cellar?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: When I left the basement, I just went outside in the yard in front of the house to see them from the other side, here. I was not able to stay there longer because of the bullets.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I ask the usher to assist this witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you point or mark with the marker where you went when you were leaving the cellar?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: This direction here, in front of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And what could you see from that direction or when you went to that spot?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I could hear the gunshots. The houses that were torched in the morning at 8.00 on the other side of the village, where the bus-stop is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And just for clarification, how far from the line or from the -- it looks like a terrace, how far did you go to the spot where you had that view, if you could just tell?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Not very far. Up to here, maybe two or three metres further from the basement; not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you draw an arrow to the direction where you went, because I understand it might not be depicted on this picture?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I cannot see the arrow here. Can you maybe try it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, if this latest drawing could be erased a little bit, so we can see clearly an arrow.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I think you can see it now, from here to here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I suggest that be marked with the number 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you say again the view you had from that spot? What could you see from there?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: On that Sunday, I could see the fire coming from the torched houses. I could hear the gunshots.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where are the torched houses?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: On the right side of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And by "village," you refer to Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: My colleague has asked you about vehicles. Did you see any vehicles on that Sunday, the 12th of August in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, two armoured vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where did you see them?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: One, when they came to the main street of where we were, and they know it very well, how many were there; but I saw two, two Hermelin cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I just clarify "the main street of where we were," what street are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: The main street here. They came from this side, the road above here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Does that street have a particular name?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I think that this road takes you to the Macedonian village called Rastak.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you saw them on the street outside the yard, which is depicted on this picture, yes?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. And we could hear the noise.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You stated - and this is page 67, line 4 - "When they came to the main street." Whom are you referring to by "they"?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: The Macedonian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You were asked about the village leader, Kenan Saliu, and the village leader, Mr. Saliu, had helped arrange an interview by the ICTY. My question to you is: To your knowledge, did at any point in time the Macedonian police approach Mr. Kenan Saliu in order to arrange an interview with you?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Have you been approached or not?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I just clarify this one point. Do you know whether the police ever approached Mr. Kenan Saliu in order to arrange an interview with you?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: This I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. You were also asked whether you supported the NLA in 2001. Is it fair to say that in your heart you did support the NLA in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, from my heart, but I did not participate in any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before we finish with the witness, the photograph on the screen in front of you, does the position that you went to from where you could see the fire of the houses and other things, is that position shown on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. It's in front of the house, here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that where you have marked the head of the arrow or is it some other position?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I can't see what you're pointing to, unfortunately. Can you see the arrow-head that you've drawn, the red one?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that the position you're pointing to or are you pointing to some other position?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, this is the location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you mark that with a number 4, please.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You did mention the main street, the street you thought that led to Rastak. Is that a street that goes by the front of this house?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Not in front, but behind the house. If you can see this wall here, it's above that wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you mark the wall with a cross, please.

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: Here is the wall, and behind this wall is the road that I mentioned, behind the wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you referred to Hermelin vehicles. Did you see a Hermelin vehicle on that road at any time, or on that street?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No, not earlier than Sunday, when the police forces came.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. And on the Sunday, you did see a Hermelin on that street?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I heard from others as well that there were two Hermelins present there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm wanting to learn, first of all, whether you saw any Hermelin vehicles that Sunday. Can you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I saw only one. When it passed by along this many road, I heard the roar, and it proceeded in the direction of Rastak village, and then came back, again, along the same road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you heard it. Did you see it yourself?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I both saw it and heard the noise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned in your evidence two Hermelins. Did you, on that Sunday, see a second Hermelin anywhere?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: No, I didn't see the second; but, as I said, I heard that there were two Hermelins there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And did you hear the sound with your ears, or did somebody else tell you there were two Hermelins?

utterances.speaker: ISMAIL RAMADANI
utterances.text: I did hear the sound of the first Hermelin vehicle, but not of the second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, I take it, Mr. Neuner, you want to tender this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P196, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You will be pleased to know that that concludes your evidence and the questions that are asked of you. The Chamber would thank you for coming to The Hague and for the assistance that you have been able to give us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're now free to leave and the court officer will show you out. Thank you indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Twelve or 13 minutes remain, Mr. Saxon or Mr. Neuner, whoever is dealing with the next witness. Is that useful time or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution believes that all time is useful, and Ms. Motoike will lead the next witness and we would like to begin, with the Court's permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Splendid. Then we will get the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good afternoon. The Prosecution at this time will call Osman Ramadani.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that is now given to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're glad to hear you have a good clear voice, Mr. Ramadani, and Ms. Motoike has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Ramadani.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Is your name Osman Ramadani?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And is your ethnicity Albanian?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And do you live in the village of Ljuboten in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And were you residing in Ljuboten during 10 and 12 August 2001?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And at some point have you given statements to members of my office, the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And in April of this year, 2007, you met with myself and a colleague and signed another statement that contained a consolidation of your prior statements; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honours, with the assistance of the usher, if can he could show Mr. Ramadani the hard copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: If we could show Mr. Ramadani the document, which bears ERN number N006-4092/N006-4112.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, do you see that document before you?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Is your signature there at the bottom of page 1?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if could you take a look at every single page of that document, did you sign every single page at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if could you look at page 21, there's a paragraph on that page.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: On page 21, there is a paragraph that has the title in English, "Witness Acknowledgement." Is that your signature there underneath that, "Witness Acknowledgment"?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And after you signed this statement, did you then make some corrections and/or additions to this statement at that time?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, if can we could show Mr. Ramadani the next document, which bears ERN N006-4078/N006-4090.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Mr. Ramadani, do you see your signature at the bottom of page 1 of this document?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if could you take a look at page 2, at the top, it says, "Additions or Corrections to Rule 92 ter statement," in English. Is your signature at the bottom there on page 2?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And did you sign every page of this document at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And were the contents of this document read to you in your native language before you had an opportunity to sign it?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And if could you take a look at the page 13 of this particular document, where it says, "Witness Acknowledgment," is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And on the -- on 8 May, 2007, did you and I and another colleague from my office also have an opportunity to speak about these particular statements?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: At that time, did you make a correction to the name of a particular body-guard who had you mentioned in paragraph 26 of that addenda correction statement?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And what was this correction that you provided to me at that time?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: The correction was related to the body-guard.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And at that time, did you indicate that the body-guard's name was written wrong in your prior addenda correction statement?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes. It was a translation mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And the name as it appears in paragraph 26 is Goran. Is it supposed to be Blagoje?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Blagoje, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And with that correction in mind and these two particular statements, are you satisfied that these statements are correct and accurate?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, 100 per cent correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: And would these statements represent what you would say if you were asked the same questions in court today?

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: Yes, the same, no changes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask at this time to tender the consolidated 92 ter statement for Mr. Ramadani, as well as the addenda corrigenda to the 92 ter statement pursuant to Rule 92 ter; and because of some of the contents of the documents, I would ask that they be tendered under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Both will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The first statement with ERN N006-4092 will become exhibit P197. The second statement with ERN N006-4078 will become Exhibit P198, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before we pass on, can I just ask you, Mr. Ramadani, how many brothers do you have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have two brothers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: They are Beqir and Ismail? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: OSMAN RAMADANI
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is a reference to paragraph 2 of Exhibit 197, which is confusing. Yes, Ms. Motoike.

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. With the Chamber's permission, I will read a brief summary of this particular witness's statements. The witness, Mr. Ramadani, is a Macedonian of Albanian ethnicity who was born there Ljuboten where he has resided all his life. On 12 August 2001, military forces and police, including the Lions, detained the witness and other Ljuboten villagers outside of a house, where they had sought refuge in the basement, and this basement is the same basement that other witnesses have testified to. The witness was severely beaten and mistreated by the police, and Sulejman Bajrami was shot and killed at that location. The witness and other detainees were then forcefully marched to Brace's House, where the witness saw Mr. Ljube Boskoski. The witness was beaten and mistreated whilst walking to Brace's House and also upon his arrival there. He was subsequently detained at Mirkovci police station for two to three days, where the witness and other detainees were beaten by police officers. The witness was also taken to Skopje Court II, where he was forced to sign a document, and then he was transferred to Sutka prison. At the prison, he received more beatings by the guards, resulting in his hospitalisation at Skopje city hospital. The witness was then returned to prison where he remained for four months. The witness saw no NLA presentation in Ljuboten on 10 to 12 August, 2001, and he later learned that his father, Muharem Ramadani, and three cousins were killed during the attack on 12 August 2001. Your Honours, I see the hour at this point. I don't know whether or not the Court would like me to go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're in a position of moving on to some new topic now, are you?

utterances.speaker: MS. MOTOIKE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, then I think we break now and we resume tomorrow at 9.00 a.m. Sir, I'm sorry that you only just got started, but we have now to finish for the day and your evidence will continue tomorrow morning at 9.00 a.m. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
